Quod omnis Inimicicia, Rancor, cordis, odium, et locucio, que inter nos et vsque in hodiernum diem ex parte vna, et Nobiles seu famosos viros dominum Petrum de Rosenberch et amicos suos ex parte altera est habita, nunc ex amicabili composicione, et perpetua vnione quam fauente domino mutuis affectibus, inimus presentibus et confederamus consistit suffocata, prorsus mortua et sepulta. Promittentes sub nostre fidei puritate, vnacum Illustri Principe domino Boleslao Duce Silezie domino in Legnicz, amicisque nostris dominis, Wilelmo de Lantstein Pothone de Fridlant, Hinkone Berka domino Glacensi, Hinkone de Huska fratribus, nostrisque filiis Heinrico et Czenkone de Lipa, qui spondent nobiscum, et pro nobis, dicto domino Petro de Rosenberch ac suis amicis perpetuam amiciciam adimplere, ipsumque iuuare quoad uixerimus, contra quemlibet hominem cuiuscumque condicionis fuerit qui eum et amicos suos contra deum et iusticiam niteretur destruere uel molestare, dumtaxat excepto domino nostro Rege cui astabimus prout homagium fidei nostre postulat, et requirit. Sin autem dictus dominus noster Rex, nominatum dominum Petrum vel amicos suos conaretur destruere, aut adnichilare contra deum et iusti ciam, ex tunc nos promittimus sine omni fraude, prefatum dominum Petrum et amicos suos iuuare rebus pariter et personis, et ipsos non deserere in omni iusticia et veritate. entries.english:
Henry von Lipa, together with his sons Henry and Čeněk, promises that, after ending the enmity which had long existed between them and Peter von Rosenberg and his friends, they will assist Peter and his party against any person. Given at Prague on the feast of Saint Mark the Evangelist, 1316.

Dietrich and Heinrich von Fällstein, canons of Olomouc and lords zu Hochwald, transfer the advocacy of Budišov to the purchaser Walter, citizen of Olomouc, 1316.

Hermann, abbot of Žabrdovice, gives certain vineyards at Šatov to the convent of Louka.

CI. We, Henry von Lipa, make known to all, present and future, to whom this charter is shown, that all enmity, resentment, hatred, and hostile speech which until this day has existed on the one side between us and on the other side the noble and distinguished lord Peter von Rosenberg and his friends is now, through a friendly settlement and lasting union which, with the Lord’s favor and mutual goodwill, we have entered into and established by this charter, stifled, entirely dead, and buried.

In good faith we promise, together with the illustrious prince Lord Boleslaus, Duke of Silesia and lord of Legnica, and our friends, Lords William von Landstein, Pothon von Friedland, Hinko Berka, lord of Glatz, the brothers Hinko von Houska, and our sons Henry and Čeněk von Lipa, who pledge themselves with us and on our behalf, to maintain lasting friendship with the aforesaid Lord Peter von Rosenberg and his friends. For as long as we live, we will assist him against any person, whatever his standing, who seeks to destroy or molest him and his friends contrary to God and justice. We except only our lord the King, whom we shall support as our homage and fidelity require. But if our said lord the King should seek to destroy or annihilate the aforesaid Lord Peter or his friends contrary to God and justice, then we promise without deceit to assist Lord Peter and his friends with both our resources and our persons, and not to abandon them in any matter of justice and truth.

Furthermore, if fortune smiles upon us and our said lord the King favors us with special grace, we promise faithfully to promote before the King the welfare and advantage of Lord Peter and his friends as if it were our own. If any of our friends should in any way wrong Lord Peter or his friends, then Lord Peter or his friends must bring the matter to our attention. We shall ensure that the offense is corrected immediately and that, on our advice, worthy compensation is made to Lord Peter and his friends.

If, which God forbid, we fail in any part or in the whole of the friendship and union promised above to Lord Peter and his friends, then we wish to be declared perjurers, oath-breakers, and outlaws. Moreover, the aforesaid lords—the illustrious Duke of Silesia and our friends who have pledged themselves on our behalf—shall be bound to assist Lord Peter and his friends against us faithfully with all their power and to seek our harm in every way.

In witness of this, we have had this letter written and secured with the force of our seals. Done and given at Prague in the year of the Lord 1316, on the feast of Saint Mark the Evangelist.

[Copied by A. Boczek from the original, with eight seals, in the Třeboň archive, no. N. 3.]

CII. Dietrich and Heinrich von Fällstein, canons of Olomouc and lords zu Hochwald, transfer the advocacy of Budišov to the purchaser Walter, citizen of Olomouc, 1316.

In God’s name, amen. Since human deeds pass with time into oblivion, it is fitting to secure them with documents. Therefore we, Lords Dietrich and Heinrich von Wildenstein, canons of Olomouc and lords zu Hochwald, publicly declare in this charter that we give and sell to our dear and faithful Walter the advocacy of Budišov, for him, his children, and all his heirs, with all the rights that belong to it, in return for his faithful service to us.

First, we give him three hides of arable land and a quarter hide of peas; and as service land, one hide in exchange for three morgens, one hide in exchange for two morgens, and one hide in exchange for one morgen. We give him a free gardener and an annual rent of four groschen, payable on one hide on Saint Michael’s Day. We also give him a right to establish a free butcher’s stall near the town, six butcher’s stalls, six bread stalls, six shoe stalls, and a free bathhouse. We give him a mill below the town with two wheels, and a mill above the town with one wheel on the water called the Budišov. In addition, for love of him, we give him the right to build a mill in half the village with two wheels, since the water in the Budišov is low and often fails.

We give him the court in half the village with all its rights and every kind of fishery, together with the hide of arable land mentioned above. We assign to the advocacy all meadows and all woods belonging to that court. We give him bees in the forest and the right to make clearings wherever he can or may in the forest by the water called the Lopnice. The forest belonging to the town of Budišov is not included: no trees may be cut there without the town’s permission, whether on the town’s account or the advocate’s, and neither side may take anything from the other. A forest on the Oder, which also belongs to the town, is included as far as its boundaries extend, with the same right to make clearings. For this, the advocate shall serve with a crossbow or as a marksman.

We further grant our advocate the right to hold court with our burgrave or our land advocate. For cases involving manslaughter, cries of murder, limbs, wounds, rape, or violence, we give him one third of the fine, according to our assessment. He shall have the right to collect the lesser fines. We grant him the right to hold court with our land advocate beneath the four lindens, four times a year, and to receive two hellers each year from every house for this purpose. Those four judges may not act without the advocate’s permission. He shall have and exercise all rights and powers in the town, and for love of him we grant him freedom to hunt all kinds of large game.

In confirmation of this charter, we have attached our seal. Given at Olomouc in the year of Our Lord 1316.

[Translated from the feudal-table regest no. III, p. 41, in the archiepiscopal archive at Kroměříž by Dr. G. Branowitzer.]

CIII. Hermann, abbot of Žabrdovice, gives certain vineyards at Šatov to the convent of Louka. Done at Louka on 30 May 1316.

We, Hermann, by divine mercy abbot of the Premonstratensian monastery of Žabrdovice in the diocese of Olomouc, make known to all who see this letter that we freely transfer to our brethren, the convent of Louka, for their perpetual refectory endowment, the vineyards we own at Šatov on the Count’s Hill, one of which is called Regis and the other is now called Antiqua Crucifera. We bought them with our own money through the diligence of our venerable brother John, formerly our abbot, on the condition that we might assign them permanently to the refectory of the brethren of that convent whenever we wished, with the consent of the aforesaid lord abbot of Louka.

Accordingly, we now freely transfer those vineyards to the same brethren, for their refectory. We, John, by the same divine mercy abbot of Louka, confirm as a permanent endowment for the refectory of our beloved brethren this donation made by our aforesaid venerable brother, Lord Hermann, abbot of Žabrdovice, and acknowledge it as having been made from the beginning. In witness of this, we have authenticated this letter with our seals. Given at Louka in the year of the Lord 1316, on the third day before the Kalends of June.

[Original parchment with two broken seals in the archive of the monastery of Louka at C. B. Gubern., Brno, under H. no. 13.]
